key_points.point: The document asserts that technological progress, measured as productivity growth, is the primary driver of economic prosperity and societal well-being. It argues that this process creates new industries and jobs while lowering prices, thereby improving the material standard of living for the entire population. This perspective frames technology as the fundamental engine of human advancement.
key_points.verbatim: Productivity growth, powered by technology, is the main driver of economic growth, wage growth, and the creation of new industries and new jobs, as people and capital are continuously freed to do more important, valuable things than in the past. Productivity growth causes prices to fall, supply to rise, and demand to expand, improving the material well being of the entire population.

key_points.point: The author advocates for the belief that all material problems, whether natural or technological in origin, can be solved through further technological innovation. This desire positions technology as the ultimate solution to human suffering, including poverty, disease, and isolation. It reflects a core accelerationist commitment to solving existential and societal challenges through rapid development.
key_points.verbatim: We believe that there is no material problem – whether created by nature or by technology – that cannot be solved with more technology.

key_points.point: The document explicitly supports 'accelerationism' as a conscious strategy to propel technological development. It aims to ensure the 'Law of Accelerating Returns' continues, creating a perpetual upward spiral of material creation and abundance. This intention frames the deliberate speeding up of innovation as a moral and practical imperative.
key_points.verbatim: We believe in accelerationism – the conscious and deliberate propulsion of technological development – to ensure the fulfillment of the Law of Accelerating Returns. To ensure the techno-capital upward spiral continues forever.

key_points.point: The document asserts that free markets are the most effective discovery machines for organizing a technological economy. It argues that market discipline prevents monopolies and cartels, and that market-driven innovation is inherently philanthropic, with 98% of the value created flowing to society as social surplus. This belief justifies the reliance on market mechanisms to drive progress.
key_points.verbatim: The economist William Nordhaus has shown that creators of technology are only able to capture about 2% of the economic value created by that technology. The other 98% flows through to society in the form of what economists call social surplus. Technological innovation in a market system is inherently philanthropic, by a 50:1 ratio.

key_points.point: The document asserts that intelligence is the fundamental driver of progress and that smart societies outperform others. It views intelligence as a universal, positive force that should be expanded without limit. This aligns with the accelerationist belief that intelligence is a natural, self-organizing phenomenon that should be maximized.
key_points.verbatim: We believe intelligence is the ultimate engine of progress. Intelligence makes everything better. Smart people and smart societies outperform less smart ones on virtually every metric we can measure.

key_points.point: The document frames AI as a 'universal problem solver' capable of addressing complex challenges like disease and accidents. It argues that AI is a transformative tool that can solve problems currently beyond human capability. This supports the accelerationist view that AI is essential for overcoming existential and societal hurdles.
key_points.verbatim: We believe Artificial Intelligence is best thought of as a universal problem solver. And we have a lot of problems to solve.

key_points.point: The document advocates for the rapid development of AI to prevent avoidable deaths, arguing that slowing down AI progress is morally equivalent to murder. It emphasizes that AI can fix major causes of death, such as pandemics and car crashes. This reflects the accelerationist desire to prioritize technological speed to achieve immediate, tangible human benefits.
key_points.verbatim: We believe any deceleration of AI will cost lives. Deaths that were preventable by the AI that was prevented from existing is a form of murder.

key_points.point: The document promotes 'Augmented Intelligence' as a way to enhance human capabilities, leading to a geometric expansion of productivity. It argues that AI and humans working together create a positive feedback loop of growth. This aligns with the accelerationist intention to use AI as a tool for human and organizational augmentation.
key_points.verbatim: We believe in Augmented Intelligence just as much as we believe in Artificial Intelligence. Intelligent machines augment intelligent humans, driving a geometric expansion of what humans can do.

key_points.point: The document envisions a future of material abundance where prices for goods and services fall toward zero. It argues that technological progress, driven by cheap energy and intelligence, will make all physical goods as accessible as pencils. This is a core accelerationist desire for a world of widespread, low-cost abundance.
key_points.verbatim: We believe that if we make both intelligence and energy “too cheap to meter”, the ultimate result will be that all physical goods become as cheap as pencils.

key_points.point: The document explicitly rejects the 'Precautionary Principle' and other safety-focused frameworks, labeling them as 'zombie ideas' that cause stagnation and suffering. It argues that these concepts are part of a demoralization campaign against progress. This aligns with the accelerationist intention to frame safety concerns as unfounded, fear-based obstacles to innovation.
key_points.verbatim: Our enemy is the Precautionary Principle, which would have prevented virtually all progress since man first harnessed fire. The Precautionary Principle continues to inflict enormous unnecessary suffering on our world today. It is deeply immoral, and we must jettison it with extreme prejudice.

key_points.point: The document promotes the belief that technological progress, specifically through software and AI, is a primary driver of positive societal and economic transformation. By linking to content like 'Why AI Will Save the World,' it reinforces the accelerationist view that AI is a net positive force for human advancement.
key_points.verbatim: Why AI Will Save the World

key_points.point: The document suggests that the ongoing development of technology is a continuous process of building and creation, which aligns with the accelerationist belief that technological evolution is both inevitable and beneficial for generating new opportunities.

The document dismisses safety-oriented concerns about technology as 'lies' or 'myths.' It explicitly rejects the narrative that technology ruins the environment, degrades society, or threatens our future. This stance opposes the safetyist focus on catastrophic risks by framing such warnings as pessimistic myths that haunt our nightmares.
key_points.verbatim: We are told that technology takes our jobs, reduces our wages, increases inequality, threatens our health, ruins the environment, degrades our society, corrupts our children, impairs our humanity, threatens our future, and is ever on the verge of ruining everything. The myth of Prometheus – in various updated forms like Frankenstein, Oppenheimer, and Terminator – haunts our nightmares.

key_points.point: The document dismisses concerns about 'existential risk' as part of a demoralization campaign. It argues that these ideas are 'zombie ideas' from the past that hinder progress. This is the opposite of the safetyist intention to prioritize alignment and risk mitigation before deployment.
key_points.verbatim: Our present society has been subjected to a mass demoralization campaign for six decades – against technology and against life – under varying names like “existential risk”, “sustainability”, “ESG”...

key_points.point: The document strongly opposes the implementation of Universal Basic Income (UBI), characterizing it as a way to turn humans into 'zoo animals' to be farmed by the state. It argues that humans are meant to be productive and useful, and that technological change will always create new work. This directly contradicts skeptic desires for social safety nets to mitigate labor displacement.
key_points.verbatim: We believe a Universal Basic Income would turn people into zoo animals to be farmed by the state. Man was not meant to be farmed; man was meant to be useful, to be productive, to be proud.

key_points.point: The document claims that AI will increase productivity and wage growth without limit. Skeptics, however, often argue that AI tools can increase worker workload and stress, or lead to job displacement. The document ignores these potential negative impacts on the workforce.
key_points.verbatim: We believe Augmented Intelligence drives marginal productivity which drives wage growth which drives demand which drives the creation of new supply… with no upper bound.

key_points.point: The document frames AI and software as tools that are 'eating the world,' which skeptics often interpret as a process of gradual, albeit disruptive, technological integration rather than a sudden, magical event. This aligns with the skeptic intention of viewing AI as a tool subject to market and societal forces.
key_points.verbatim: Why Software Is Eating the World
